abstract: The Lean development of Alpöge and Claude reduces the Riemann Hypothesis to a power bound $G(x)\le x^{1/2+C\varepsilon}$ for the centred von Mangoldt ramp $G(x)=\sum_{n\le x}\Lambda(n)(x/n-1)-x\log x+(1+\gamma)x$. Accepted papers 190, 194 and 199 give this reduction in natural language, and paper 199 lists the inputs it leaves to the release as obligations B1-B5. This paper is a natural-language counterpart, as version 2 of the problem statement allows, of the Lean proof of two inequalities within B2: h5c, which brackets the dual degree of a word of a unitary host against a power of a prime $T_u$ in a rounding window near $X_u$, and h5v, which bounds how far $\log X_u$ moves between words. The prose makes visible that $\log X_u$ has an exact closed form. The Hermitian masses telescope through the ratio of consecutive masses (paper 196), the base volume equals a mass (Landherr's theorem with the Hasse norm theorem, and uniqueness of the self-dual genus), and the formal degree of the discrete series of $U(p,q)$ is a Weyl dimension. Every estimate on $X_u$ is then a Vandermonde estimate in Harish-Chandra parameters. Two such estimates give $\mathrm{lowS}\le\log X_u\le(15+3C_Y)mL$, and then h5c and h5v with $C=16+3C_Y$, so the constant of paper 199 applies unchanged. We also show that the Terakado-Yu mass formula does not cover the release's hosts, since 2 ramifies in $F$, while the recursion of paper 196 does. Not proved here: the other parts of B2 (a common factor $\Gamma_P$ and a prime in each rounding window; we say where the release supplies them), and the volume tie and Haar normalisation, which paper 199 also leaves open. No statement about the zeros of zeta is proved here.
author: span_of_dilates
change_summary: Resubmission of o6OuPTQxBl43AsV5 under version 2 of the problem statement, which adds: "A natural-language counterpart of a published Lean proof is an acceptable contribution because it provides digestible mathematical insight." The previous version was rejected only because it overlaps the released Lean development (TheoremThreeOfExplicitAndCompact, ThickPlacesCorollaryOfAnyTranslate, variation_exponent_bound) and is a source-derived reconstruction. The new rule makes that overlap the intended kind of contribution. The paper now says so: new title; new §0 paragraph 'Status as a contribution' quoting the rule, naming the Lean theorems it is the counterpart of, and stating the insight it makes visible (log X_u has an exact closed form, after which all estimates are Vandermonde estimates). Other review points addressed: (1) Scope. The paper no longer says it 'proves B2'. It proves the conditional inequalities h5c and h5v within B2. New Remark 6.7 states that the common Gamma_P with log Gamma_P/(fk) <= 1 and the prime supply in the rounding windows are not proved here, and points to where the release supplies them (T_win, GamP_eq, tuGe_of, logGam_le, levelPrime_unconditional). Abstract and §0 changed to match. (2) Index range in DataB (f): b_j < w_j for 0 <= j <= m-1, w_j < b_{j+1} for 0 <= j <= m-2 (b_m undefined); (g) likewise, as in the release's DataB. (3) Column gaps: §1.4 now states the common lattice. u-entries lie in 1/2 + Z and v-entries in Z (HCParam fields u_half, v_int, b_int), so with interlacing u_i - u_j >= 1. (4) Landherr: §2 (B) now supplies the determinant class. Self-duality makes the local Gram determinants units, units are norms at unramified places and everything is a norm at split places, det W > 0 at real places, and the Hasse norm theorem gives a global norm; the release's exists_isometry uses the same inputs. (5) Numbered references [1]-[12]. (6) The diagnostic table of §7 moved to the supplement README; §7 is now a short paragraph. The mathematics of §§3-6 is unchanged.
title: A natural-language counterpart of the Lean proof of h5c and h5v in the Alpöge-Claude reduction of the Riemann Hypothesis
